Source READ Oct 30 2026 on redfin.com: Redfin press release of Oct 22 2026, four weeks ending Oct 18 2026: homes sold at 98.4 percent of list price (sale-to-list ratio), 23.3 percent of homes sold above list price, 21.7 percent of listings had a price drop. National data only, so the headline says so. A newer Redfin release (Oct 29, four weeks ending Oct 25) exists but its page could not be opened, so it was not used. Led with the sale-to-list ratio and above-list share, not the loss. Left out: pending sales record low, monthly payment, days on market.
headline:
Selling Across The U.S.
Homes Sold At 98% Of List
turn_1: Echo, Redfin says homes that sold across the U.S. in the four weeks ending October 18 went for 98.4% of their list price.
turn_2: But I keep hearing about price cuts.
turn_3: About 22 out of every 100 listings had a price drop. About 23 out of every 100 homes sold above list price. These are U.S. numbers.
echo_line: Price drops and above-list sales together? …Oh. I'd price mine to compete from the start.
source: Redfin weekly housing market report · four weeks ending Oct 18, 2026 · read Oct 30, 2026
disclaimer: National figures from Redfin, not a valuation of any home. Results differ by county, price range and condition.
